title: Successive enumeration rounds
statement: Let $f$ and the two Boolean oracles satisfy, for every Boolean word $x$ and natural number $j$, $o_0(\langle x,\operatorname{bits}(j)\rangle)$ is true exactly when $j<|f(x)|$, and $o_1(\langle x,\operatorname{bits}(j)\rangle)$ equals the $j$-th bit of $f(x)$, defaulting to false when absent. Suppose $|f(x)|\le F$, and $|\operatorname{bits}(j+1)|\le W$ for every $j<|f(x)|$. For every $i\le |f(x)|$, the enumerator has a finite run from its initial configuration with empty output and counter zero to a configuration with the first $i$ bits of $f(x)$ as output, state asking, and counter $i$; every configuration strictly before the end of this run has shape bounded by $F$ and $W$.
hypotheses_covered: The length oracle correctly tests whether an index is below the output length
The bit oracle returns the output bit, defaulting to false when absent
The output length is at most $F$
For every index below the output length, the bit length of its successor is at most $W$
